text:
devon: FYI — seeing a big provisioning backlog in eu-central-1 (CT1). Control plane shows queued GPU allocations + KMS auth timeouts. Also getting higher 503/504s from CDN for model shards. filing here before pager hits.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-CT1-NET-KMS (P2) — https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-CT1-NET-KMS :rotating_light:
ian: what's the scope? production inference impact or just onboarding/dedicated pools?
maya: production hostgroups for hosted-api are seeing latencies. Autoscaler has 420 pending pods, many stuck in Init because disk mount fails during decrypt step.
lisa: seeing KMS timeouts in node bootstrap logs:
```
2026-03-18T09:04:12Z boot.sh: kms: request failed: timeout after 10s
2026-03-18T09:04:13Z mount: /dev/nvme1n1: failed to decrypt: KMS_EGRESS_ERR
```
cloud-eng: provider status page (https://status.cloudprov.example) shows a networking degradation in eu-central affecting control-plane <-> kms endpoints and edge-cdn POPs. They report BGP reconvergence in progress.
nate: CDN 503s are spiking for certain edge nodes — that explains shard fetch failures and increased tail latency for streaming responses.
ian: impact: API 95th p50->p95 jump, some in-region requests failing. Any immediate mitigation ideas?
maya: two-prong: 1) reduce new allocations in CT1 (stop autoscaler from creating new GPU nodes), 2) failover routing for new traffic to eu-west-1 warm pool.
lisa: we can also change instance bootstrap to use fallback KMS endpoint in another region. small code change to init script:
```
KMS_ENDPOINTS=("kms.eu-central-1.cloudprov" "kms.eu-west-1.cloudprov")
for e in "${KMS_ENDPOINTS[@]}"; do attempt_kms_fetch && break; done
```
devon: can we roll that change to existing queued nodes so they can finish init without redeploys?
cloud-eng: short answer: no, init runs on first boot. But we can abort and re-run provisioning with the patched image for the queued jobs. That will cost extra hours but unblocks capacity.
ian: cost vs user impact — prefer targeted traffic shift first. set target 20% -> eu-west-1 for non-critical routes and 100% -> eu-west for new sessions until CT1 healthy.
nate: I can update the global router. Suggest gradual ramp: 10% then 30% then 60% with 5m intervals, watch error budget.
maya: also throttling background batch jobs and preemptible training jobs in CT1 frees up ~120 GPUs within 25m.
lisa: note: some dedicated pools are pinned to CT1 for compliance customers — we must not evict those.
ian: make a runbook: (A) pause autoscaler in CT1 (maya) (B) route new traffic to eu-west warm pool (nate) (C) pause non-critical batch jobs (maya) (D) prepare patched image with fallback KMS and redeploy queued (lisa/cloud-eng) (E) monitor metrics and CDN error rate (devon)
maya: pausing autoscaler now -> applied: `kubectl patch cm autoscaler-config -p '{"spec": {"enabled": false}}'` :white_check_mark:
nate: changing global router to start 10% -> eu-west-1 now. watching.
ops-bot: deployment job 4521 started: warm-pool-promote -> eu-west-1 (canary)
lisa: building patched image with fallback KMS and increasing KMS client retries. pushing to staging.
cloud-eng: heads-up: a quick workaround is to allow node bootstrap to use local ephemeral encryption key fallback for ephemeral volumes (no CMK). security says ok for non-customer-data pools. That would massively reduce KMS dependency for boot.
ian: authorize ephemeral fallback for non-sensitive pools only. Maya, list pools that can use it.
maya: affected pools marked: hosted-spot, batch-gpu, preemptible-train — applying ephemeral fallback to those now.
nate: eu-west can handle current redirected load. CDN errors decreased slightly after shift: 503 rate from 12% -> 6% in the last 5m.
devon: queued provisioning numbers dropping from 420 -> 140 after autoscaler pause + batch throttle + traffic shift. good trend.
lisa: patched image pushed. initiating restart for 90 queued instances in CT1 with the new image. script:
```
for id in $(cat queued_ids.txt); do provctl reprovision $id --image redwood/init-fallback:2026-03-18; done
```
cloud-eng: note that reprovision will consume extra credits since nodes will boot twice. budgeting FYI.
ops-bot: note added to incident TIMELINE: autoscaler pause, traffic shift, ephemeral fallback enabled for non-customer pools, reprovisioning queued nodes.
ian: agreed next steps: continue ramp to 50% if metrics remain stable, complete reprovision run, then allow autoscaler to slowly resume once KMS latencies < 200ms.
maya: reprovisioning run started. ETA ~35m for all queued nodes to finish boot validation.
devon: monitoring: request success rate improving, p95 latency trending down. CDN 503s at 3% now.
nate: global router ramp to 35% -> eu-west now.
lisa: reminder: need follow-up to harden boot sequence. Propose fallback KMS endpoint baked into AMIs and 3x retry with exponential backoff.
ian: assigning postmortem: devon owner, lisa tech lead, cloud-eng for remediation plan. severity review scheduled in 48h.
devon: thanks everyone. keeping channel open. if anything spikes re-pager to P1.
ops-bot: incident update: status -> mitigated. next: postmortem will be filed by devon within 72h. :white_check_mark:
